Poultry Farm Guide · Langley, BC
Quota, barns & ALR land —
what the numbers actually look like.

A poultry farm is four assets stapled together: the land, the barns, the quota, and the grower agreement with a processor. Each one is priced differently and each one transfers differently. Most buyers who lose a deal here lose it on the quota transfer, not the financing.

BC Egg Quota Exchange
Quota Is the Part That Sets the Price
Chicken, turkey and table eggs are all supply managed. You cannot grow at commercial scale without quota, and quota is not something you buy at a title company.

Every transfer needs marketing board approval, and the growing site itself has to be inspected and approved before birds go in. The three sectors work differently, and that difference decides how a Langley farm gets sold.
Chicken
Broilers
No central exchange.
Quota moves privately, through hatchery and processor relationships, direct grower contact, or word of mouth. That is precisely why so many broiler farms here trade off-market and never touch MLS.
Table Eggs
Layers
Published clearing price.
BC Egg runs a formal quota exchange. The June 2026 exchange cleared at $365 per unit, one unit being one bird space. It is the only sector where you can look up the number yourself.
Turkey
Meat birds
Measured in kilograms

of annual production rather than bird spaces. Allocation can be leased out, but only for a maximum of two consecutive quota years unless the board orders otherwise, which matters if a seller is running on leased allocation.

Two practical consequences. Quota is usually the largest single line in the purchase price and is not covered by a standard residential appraisal. And an accepted offer is not a closed deal until the board approves both the transfer and the site, so the subject clauses have to be written for that reality.
Barns Are the Second Valuation

Two farms with identical quota can be a million dollars apart on barn condition. Most buyers price the quota carefully and then eyeball the buildings. Here is what to actually verify before you write.
Barn age, span and floor area
Usable square footage per bird decides how much of the quota can actually be filled. Older narrow-span barns often cannot house the quota attached to the title.
Ventilation type
Tunnel ventilation with cool cells versus natural or cross ventilation. Fraser Valley heat events have made this a production issue, not a comfort issue.
Backup power
Standby generator size, transfer switch, service records. A ventilation failure is a total-flock event, and insurers and lenders both ask.
Water supply
Well yield and potability testing, or municipal connection. Peak-day demand for a full barn runs far above what a residential well is built for.
Manure storage
Storage capacity, setbacks from watercourses, and compliance with BC agricultural environmental management rules. Remediation lands on the buyer.
Biosecurity layout
Controlled access, anteroom, vehicle routing, distance to neighbouring flocks. This is now a condition of doing business with processors.
Feed system and silos
Silo count and capacity, auger condition, and whether the setup matches the delivery schedule your processor runs.
Siting and flyway exposure
The valley sits on the Pacific flyway and avian influenza has hit repeatedly since 2004. Standing water, open feed, and flock density nearby all affect risk and resale.
Financing, Tax and Structure
Financing is not a mortgage.

Residential lenders generally will not finance a working farm. Buyers here use Farm Credit Canada, an agricultural lending desk at a credit union, or vendor financing on part of the quota. Expect a larger down payment than a house, an appraisal by an accredited agricultural appraiser, and a lender that wants the grower agreement and production history before it commits.
Farm class assessment

through BC Assessment requires meeting minimum gross income thresholds by parcel size, and losing farm class is an expensive surprise. GST treatment on the farmland and quota portions of a sale is not the same as on a home, and the lifetime capital gains exemption on qualified farm property is significant for sellers who plan ahead of listing. Use an accountant who does farm files specifically. This page is general information, not tax or legal advice.
Common Questions
How much does a poultry farm in Langley cost?
Prices depend far more on
quota holdings and barn infrastructure

than on land size alone. A turn-key operation with substantial quota, modern barns and level ALR acreage sits well above raw farmland value, because the supply-managed income is tied to the quota rather than the dirt.
Because most sales are off-market and quota values shift, the only reliable number is a current one. Call or text Jared Gibbons at
for a confidential valuation on a specific property.
How much does poultry quota cost in BC?
Layer quota has a published number. BC Egg runs a formal quota exchange, and the
June 2026 exchange cleared at $365 per unit
, one unit being one bird space.

Chicken and turkey quota have no published clearing price because they trade privately. Value is established from recent comparable transfers rather than a public index, which is one of the main reasons to work with someone who sees those transactions.
How does quota transfer when I buy a Langley poultry farm?
Quota is the right to produce chicken, turkey or eggs under BC's supply-management system, administered by the
BC Chicken Marketing Board
BC Turkey Marketing Board
and
BC Egg Marketing Board
. Broiler-breeder operations fall under the BC Broiler Hatching Egg Commission.

Quota does not simply run with the land. Any transfer must be applied for by both parties and approved by the applicable board, the growing site itself must be inspected and approved, and quota is not included in a sale unless expressly stated in the Contract of Purchase and Sale. See the
guide to buying a chicken farm in BC
for how the process runs start to finish.
Is the quota always included in the sale price?
No. Some farms sell with quota. Some sell as land and barns with the quota retained or already transferred elsewhere. Some sell as a share purchase of the farm corporation.
The three structures produce very different tax outcomes and very different prices. Always confirm which one you are looking at before comparing two listings side by side.
Can I finance a poultry farm with a regular mortgage?
Generally no. Residential lenders will not finance a working supply-managed farm. Buyers use
Farm Credit Canada
, an agricultural lending desk at a credit union, or vendor financing on part of the quota.

Quota is routinely used as security by agricultural lenders, though never by residential ones. Expect a larger down payment than a house and an appraisal by an accredited agricultural appraiser. Line up financing before you write, not after.
How many birds can I raise without quota?
Up to
200 birds a year

for personal use, subject to local bylaws. Between 200 and 2,000 birds a year there are small-lot permit programs through the marketing boards, aimed at farm-gate and direct-marketed production. Above that you are in the commercial quota system.
Buyers in that middle band are usually better served by
general Langley farm and acreage listings
than by hunting for a quota farm, and they still get ALR tax treatment and existing barn infrastructure.
Why is Langley a strong location for a poultry farm?
The Fraser Valley holds roughly
80 percent of BC's poultry farms
, and Langley sits inside that cluster with processors, hatcheries and feed mills close by. About three-quarters of the Township is within the ALR.

For an operator, a large level ALR parcel gives room for barn footprint, biosecurity setbacks, truck access, feed and manure handling, drainage and future expansion. Those parcels are scarce: 73 percent of Township of Langley ALR parcels are under 10 acres and only 14 percent exceed 20 acres. That scarcity is a large part of why well-configured poultry acreage holds its value.
How many acres do I need for a poultry farm?
Less than most buyers assume for the barns themselves, and more than they assume once you account for setbacks, manure storage, turnaround room for feed trucks and catch crews, and the residence.
Langley's real constraint is not total acreage. It is flat, well-drained, road-accessible parcels large enough to site a modern barn without fighting setbacks.
Can I subdivide ALR land or add a second home?

ALR subdivision requires Agricultural Land Commission approval and is rarely granted. Additional residences are governed by both the ALC and Township of Langley bylaws, with limits on size and siting.
Verify the specific parcel before assuming anything. These rules have changed more than once in recent years, and what a neighbour was allowed to build five years ago is not a reliable guide.
What kinds of poultry farms are available near Langley?
The Fraser Valley market spans several sectors, each with its own quota board and barn requirements. Browse by type:
Most regional inventory sits in
Abbotsford
and
Chilliwack
, so buyers flexible on location have considerably more to choose from. Or see

Are there off-market poultry farms for sale in Langley?
Yes, and it is the norm rather than the exception.

There is no central quota exchange for chicken in BC. Quota moves privately through hatchery and processor relationships, direct grower contact, or word of mouth, so a large share of sales never reach public listings.

If a listings page shows nothing, that is a signal to get on the off-market list, not a signal that nothing is trading. Jared maintains relationships across chicken, turkey, egg and broiler-hatching-egg operators. Call or text
